newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai newspaper urges easing of rights rules.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai newspaper urges easing of rights rules.

text.p: Shanghai's leading stock newspaper on Tuesday urged securities authorities to relax rules governing rights issues by listed companies, saying the current restrictions hindered business development.

The Shanghai Securities News said many good firms were prevented from expanding by the requirement that firms provide returns at about the rate of one-year fixed bank deposits for three years in a row before they are allowed to make a rights issue.

In addition, the restrictions make it difficult for companies with poor results to attempt a recovery through expansion on the basis of funds injected through rights issues, the newspaper said in a commentary.
Another precondition barring companies from making rights issues involving more than 30 percent of their outstanding shares had limited the pace of development of some blue-chip firms, it added.
